title: University of Konstanz Zukunftskolleg Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027: Four Fully Funded 2-Year Research Positions in Germany
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 Zukunftskolleg Postdoctoral Fellowships at the University of Konstanz in Germany , offering four outstanding early-career researchers the opportunity to pursue independent research for two years within one of the University’s most interdisciplinary academic environments. The Zukunftskolleg is the Institute for Advanced Study for early-career postdoctoral researchers at the University of Konstanz . It brings together researchers from the natural sciences, humanities and social sciences and is designed to give early-career scholars the independence, institutional resources, interdisciplinary networks and professional development opportunities needed to establish their own research profiles. For the 2026 call, the Zukunftskolleg is recruiting four Postdoctoral Fellows for two-year appointments . The positions are full-time and remunerated at E13 TV-L , the German public-sector academic salary scale. The preferred starting date is 1 April 2027 . Under certain conditions, the fellowship may be extended for an additional year when the Fellow has submitted an external grant application intended to fund their own position. The opportunity is open across academic disciplines represented at the University of Konstanz. Applicants must propose an independent research project that can be appropriately affiliated with a University department. The call is particularly intended for excellent early-career researchers who demonstrate scientific excellence, research independence, teamwork and strong potential for a successful academic career. The application deadline is 12 October 2026 at 11:00 AM Central European Time (CET) . Applications and supporting materials must be submitted in English through the University of Konstanz online application portal. About the Zukunftskolleg at the University of Konstanz The Zukunftskolleg is an Institute for Advanced Study embedded within the University of Konstanz. Its model is based on giving promising early-career researchers sufficient independence to pursue ambitious projects while remaining integrated into a larger university research environment. Unlike a narrowly disciplinary postdoctoral programme, the Zukunftskolleg brings together researchers from: Natural sciences Humanities Social sciences The programme places particular emphasis on independent research, interdisciplinary and intergenerational exchange, integration across the University, and international academic connections . English is the working language of the Zukunftskolleg. This structure can be especially valuable for researchers who have completed their doctorates and are now seeking to transition from doctoral work toward a more independent scholarly profile. Four 2-Year Postdoctoral Fellowships Available The current call offers: Four two-year Postdoctoral Fellowships The positions are full-time. The official vacancy classifies the positions as: E13 TV-L This is the German collective public-service salary framework commonly used for academic research positions at public universities. The official call does not provide a single fixed euro amount because remuneration under TV-L depends on the applicable salary stage and employment circumstances. Applicants should therefore describe the opportunity as a salaried E13 TV-L postdoctoral position , rather than assigning an unofficial fixed annual salary. Preferred Starting Date The preferred start date is: 1 April 2027 The normal initial fellowship period is two years. The call also creates a possible pathway toward: 2+1 years because Fellows who apply for external funding to finance their own position may, under the Zukunftskolleg’s rules, receive financial support for an additional fellowship year while awaiting the outcome of that external grant application. Possibility of a Third Year The initial fellowship is for two years, but the Zukunftskolleg actively encourages Fellows to pursue external funding during their appointment. According to the programme information, Postdoctoral Fellows who submit an external funding or grant application covering their own position can potentially receive support for one additional fellowship year while waiting for the funding decision. This makes the fellowship not only a two-year research opportunity but also a platform for developing the external funding record required for longer-term academic independence. Full-Time Appointment The advertised positions are: Full-time However, the formal call notes that, in principle, a position may be divided into two half-time positions . Candidates interested in such an arrangement should consult the official call or contact the Zukunftskolleg directly regarding individual circumstances. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The target group consists of excellent early-career postdoctoral researchers . The Zukunftskolleg is particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate: Scientific excellence Research independence Strong teamwork Academic ambition Capacity to develop an independent research profile Potential for a successful academic career Interest in interdisciplinary exchange Applications are assessed through a two-stage international review process . Candidates are expected to be informed of the selection decision around mid-February 2027 . PhD Eligibility Window One of the most important eligibility requirements concerns the date on which the applicant received their doctorate. Normally, applicants must hold a doctoral degree granted between: 30 September 2024 and 1 October 2026 This means the fellowship is specifically targeted at researchers at a very early postdoctoral career stage. Exceptions to the Doctoral-Date Rule Earlier PhD completion dates may potentially be accepted in cases involving: Maternity leave Paternity leave Employment contracts outside academia Candidates whose doctorate falls outside the normal eligibility period but who believe one of these exceptions applies should consult the formal call and FAQs carefully. Maximum Postdoctoral Experience In practical terms, the eligibility period means the call is directed toward researchers with approximately no more than two years of postdoctoral experience under the normal timeline. The focus is therefore firmly on scholars transitioning from doctoral study into the early stages of independent academic research. Permanent Professors Are Not Eligible Applicants must not : Hold a permanent professorship Have completed a habilitation Hold an equivalent qualification such as Venia legendi The programme is intended to support researchers who have not yet reached a permanently established senior academic career stage. Candidates With External Funding May Also Apply Researchers who already have their own position funded through another programme may still be eligible if that funding can be transferred to the University of Konstanz . This allows the Zukunftskolleg to accommodate certain candidates who bring portable external funding while still seeking the Institute’s interdisciplinary research environment. Open Across Disciplines One of the strongest features of the Zukunftskolleg Postdoctoral Fellowship is its disciplinary breadth. Applicants must propose a research project that connects with: A discipline represented at the University of Konstanz. The programme is therefore not limited to one field. Potential applicants may come from the: Humanities Social sciences Natural sciences Other academic disciplines represented at the University of Konstanz Applicants should verify that an appropriate disciplinary home and potential host exist at the University before applying. Finding a Local Host at the University of Konstanz Applicants are expected to contact a potential local host among researchers at the University of Konstanz . The purpose is to ensure that the proposed project has an appropriate institutional and disciplinary affiliation. This is an important strategic step in the application process. Candidates should not simply write a research proposal and identify the University generically. Instead, they should investigate: Which department best fits the project Which faculty members work in related research areas Whether a potential host sees intellectual compatibility How the project could become integrated into departmental research The official call notes that support from a department strengthens the application . How to Approach a Potential Host Applicants should consider contacting potential hosts well before the October deadline. A concise initial message could include: Brief academic introduction Current institution PhD field and completion date Short description of the proposed postdoctoral project Explanation of the intellectual connection with the potential host Mention of the Zukunftskolleg fellowship Request to discuss possible institutional affiliation The goal should not simply be to obtain a nominal endorsement. A strong host relationship should demonstrate genuine research alignment. Relationship to the UN Sustainable Development Goals Applicants are invited to include in their motivation letter a brief reflection on how their research relates to the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals . This does not mean every project needs to be directly framed as development research. Rather, candidates can consider whether their research connects meaningfully with themes such as: Health Education Inequality Peace and institutions Climate Sustainability Gender equality Innovation Sustainable communities Responsible production International partnerships Applicants should avoid manufacturing an artificial SDG connection. The reflection will likely be stronger if it identifies a genuine relationship between the project and one or more goals. International Experience Is an Asset International teaching or research experience is considered advantageous. A strong interest in interdisciplinary research is also an asset. International experience might include: Research conducted abroad International academic collaboration Visiting research stays International conferences Teaching in another country Cross-national research projects However, the official wording describes these elements as assets rather than absolute requirements. Research Independence The fellowship is designed specifically to help researchers develop and implement their own independent research projects . Successful Fellows are expected to: Develop their project Implement the research Establish an independent research profile Engage actively with the Zukunftskolleg community Applicants should therefore demonstrate intellectual independence from their doctoral supervisors and dissertation projects. A proposal may build on previous expertise, but it should demonstrate a credible next stage in the candidate’s development as an independent researcher. Responsibilities of Zukunftskolleg Postdoctoral Fellows Successful Fellows will have several important responsibilities. Develop and Implement the Research Project The primary responsibility is to carry out the independent project proposed in the application. The fellowship provides the institutional infrastructure needed to make that project central to the Fellow’s academic work. Build an Independent Research Profile The Zukunftskolleg explicitly expects Fellows to strengthen their own scholarly identity. This may involve: Publishing research Developing collaborations Presenting at conferences Building new methodologies Preparing grant applications Expanding research networks Developing future projects Participate in Weekly Zukunftskolleg Meetings Fellows are expected to participate actively in the Zukunftskolleg’s regular weekly meetings, known as the Jour Fixe . These meetings are a key element of the Institute’s interdisciplinary model. Participants should therefore be genuinely interested in engaging with research outside their own discipline. Contribute to the Postdoctoral Community Fellows are expected to help create an active interdisciplinary community rather than focusing exclusively on their individual projects. This may involve: Discussing colleagues’ research Participating in events Building collaborations Sharing methods and ideas Contributing to joint initiatives Residence Requirement Successful Fellows must have their: Place of residence in Konstanz or the surrounding area. The fellowship is therefore not a remote postdoctoral programme . International candidates should be prepared to relocate to the Konstanz region in Germany if selected. Research Allowance Every Postdoctoral Fellow receives an: Annual research allowance The allowance may be used, for example, to support: Research assistants Equipment The official page does not state a single universal monetary amount for the allowance in the public summary. Additional Research Funding Fellows may also gain access to funding pools supporting: Cooperative projects Research assistants Travel Equipment purchases This funding structure can help researchers build projects beyond what could be achieved through salary support alone. Co-Funding Opportunities Zukunftskolleg Fellows are eligible to apply for additional co-funding opportunities available through the Institute. This may help support activities extending beyond the core fellowship budget. International Research Visits The Zukunftskolleg maintains support mechanisms for research mobility. Fellows can: Undertake temporary research visits abroad Nominate international early-career researchers for research visits to the Zukunftskolleg These opportunities help strengthen international research connections during the fellowship. Senior Fellows and Mentorship The Institute’s support structure also allows Fellows to connect with distinguished senior scholars. Through mechanisms including: Senior Fellowships Mentorship Programme Fellows can help bring experienced researchers to Konstanz and develop relationships useful to their own research and career development. Career Development Support The Zukunftskolleg provides professional development beyond direct research funding. Available support can include: Coaching Professional career counselling Grant proposal writing support Academic staff development Research support This is particularly important for early-career researchers navigating the transition from postdoctoral work toward independent academic positions. Scientific Retreat Funding Fellows may also receive financial support to organize and run a scientific retreat . This can provide an opportunity to bring collaborators together around a focused research question, network or emerging project. No Teaching Obligation An attractive feature of the fellowship is that there is: No mandatory teaching obligation. However, Fellows have the opportunity to teach in collaboration with a University of Konstanz department if doing so supports their professional development. This allows researchers to protect substantial time for research while still gaining teaching experience when strategically useful. Cluster of Excellence Affiliations Each Fellow becomes a member of both: The Zukunftskolleg A relevant University of Konstanz department Fellows may additionally become affiliated with one of the University’s Clusters of Excellence: Politics of Inequality or: Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behaviour This provides another pathway into high-level interdisciplinary research networks. The programme information also notes that up to two Cluster-Zukunftskolleg Fellowships connected with collective behaviour may be funded directly by the Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behaviour. Application Requirements Every application must contain five main components. 1. Motivation Letter Maximum length: 1 page This is an eligibility criterion. The motivation letter should explain: Why the applicant wants to join the Zukunftskolleg How the programme supports their research trajectory Why the University of Konstanz is a strong institutional fit How interdisciplinary collaboration may benefit their research Relevant connection with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, where appropriate Applicants must respect the page limit. 2. Research Proposal Maximum length: 5 pages, including references This is also an eligibility criterion. The proposal should clearly explain: Central research problem Research questions Existing scholarship Original contribution Theoretical or conceptual framework Methodology Work plan Feasibility Connection to a discipline at Konstanz Potential wider significance Because references count within the five-page maximum, applicants need to write efficiently. 3. Curriculum Vitae A complete academic CV is required. Candidates should highlight: Academic qualifications PhD completion date Publications Research projects Grants Awards Teaching International experience Conference activity Relevant methods Academic service 4. Writing Sample The writing sample may not exceed: 30 single pages This is another eligibility criterion. The writing sample should showcase the candidate’s strongest academic work. Applicants may wish to choose material that demonstrates: Research independence Analytical sophistication Methodological ability Clear academic writing Potential for future research 5. Two Reference Letters Applicants must provide: Two letters of reference The official vacancy states that only recommendation letters may be sent directly by referees to the Zukunftskolleg application email by the deadline. All other materials should be submitted through the online application portal. Page Limits Are Strict Applicants should pay extremely close attention to the page requirements. If any of the following exceed the published limits: Motivation letter Research proposal Writing sample the application will be considered ineligible and will not receive further consideration . This is not merely a stylistic recommendation. It is an eligibility condition. Application Language All applications and supporting materials must be submitted in: English English is also the working language of the Zukunftskolleg. Application Process Applications should be submitted through the official University of Konstanz online application platform. The vacancy reference number is: 2026/138 Applicants should ensure that all materials are complete and uploaded before the deadline. Apply through the University of Konstanz portal Application Deadline The final deadline is: 12 October 2026 at 11:00 AM CET Candidates should note that this is an 11:00 AM deadline , not midnight. International applicants should carefully convert the deadline into their own local time and avoid submitting at the last moment. Selection Process Applications are evaluated in a: Two-stage process by: International reviewers The programme expects candidates to be informed of the decision around: Mid-February 2027 Selected Fellows are then expected to begin around April 1, 2027. Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application 1. Secure a Potential Host Early Do not wait until October to search for a host. Identify University of Konstanz researchers whose work genuinely overlaps with your project and approach them with a concise, well-developed research concept. 2. Demonstrate Independence From Your PhD Reviewers are seeking evidence that you can develop an independent academic identity. Your postdoctoral proposal should represent a meaningful intellectual progression beyond your doctoral thesis. 3. Explain Why Konstanz Specifically Avoid writing an application that could be sent unchanged to any university. Explain why: The specific department Potential host Zukunftskolleg Relevant research networks Possible Cluster of Excellence make Konstanz uniquely appropriate for the project. 4. Use the Five Proposal Pages Strategically Because references count toward the page limit, every paragraph needs to serve a purpose. A strong structure could include: Problem and research question State of the field Proposed contribution Methods Work programme Fit with Konstanz Expected outcomes 5. Demonstrate Interdisciplinary Potential Zukunftskolleg is fundamentally interdisciplinary. Explain what other disciplines could learn from your research and what your project could gain from discussions beyond your own field. 6. Address the SDGs Thoughtfully If your research has a meaningful connection with one or more SDGs, explain it succinctly. Avoid listing several goals without explaining the substantive relationship. 7. Respect Every Formal Requirement Remember that exceeding the page limit can result in automatic ineligibility. Check: Motivation letter: maximum one page Proposal: maximum five pages including references Writing sample: maximum 30 pages Two references English-language submission October 12 deadline at 11:00 AM CET Why the Zukunftskolleg Fellowship Stands Out The Fellowship offers considerably more than a temporary research salary. Selected Fellows receive a combination of: Independent research time Salaried full-time employment Individual research allowance Access to additional project funding Research mobility International networks Mentorship Career counselling Grant-writing assistance Potential Cluster of Excellence affiliations Opportunity rather than obligation to teach A possible additional third year linked to an external funding application The structure is designed to help postdoctoral researchers make the difficult transition from completing a PhD to establishing an internationally visible and externally funded independent research career. Important Details at a Glance Host: University of Konstanz Institute: Zukunftskolleg – Institute for Advanced Study Location: Konstanz, Germany Positions: Four Duration: Two years Preferred start: April 1, 2027 Employment: Full-time Salary classification: E13 TV-L Working language: English Teaching: No teaching obligation Residence requirement: Konstanz or surrounding area Normal PhD eligibility window: September 30, 2024–October 1, 2026 Selection: Two-stage international review Expected decision: Mid-February 2027 Deadline: October 12, 2026 at 11:00 AM CET Reference: 2026/138 Application contact: zukunftskolleg-application@uni-konstanz.de Conclusion The University of Konstanz Zukunftskolleg Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027 provide an outstanding opportunity for researchers at the very beginning of their postdoctoral careers to establish independent research profiles within an internationally oriented and interdisciplinary academic environment. Four researchers will be selected for two-year full-time positions at E13 TV-L , with a preferred start date of April 1, 2027 . The programme is open across the natural sciences, social sciences and humanities, provided the proposed project connects with a discipline represented at the University of Konstanz. Fellows join both the Zukunftskolleg and a University department and may additionally connect with major research networks such as the Politics of Inequality or Collective Behaviour Clusters of Excellence. Beyond salary and research infrastructure, Fellows receive an annual research allowance, access to funding for research assistance, travel and equipment, international research-visit opportunities, mentorship, career development, grant-writing support and additional collaborative funding possibilities. There is no compulsory teaching load, although Fellows may teach if they wish to develop their experience. The normal eligibility window requires candidates to have received their doctorate between September 30, 2024 and October 1, 2026 , subject to specified exceptions for parental leave or employment outside academia. Applicants must not hold a permanent professorship or habilitation. A strong application will combine an ambitious but feasible independent research project with clear evidence of scientific excellence, an appropriate host and disciplinary connection at Konstanz, interdisciplinary potential, and a credible trajectory toward academic independence. Candidates should begin contacting potential local hosts well before preparing the final application. The deadline is October 12, 2026 at 11:00 AM CET . title: Max Planck Dissertation Writing-up Fellowships 2027 in Germany: Up to 4 Months of Funded Support for Final-Stage PhD Researchers
summary: Applications are now open for the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology Dissertation Writing-up Fellowships 2027 , offering doctoral candidates in the final stage of their PhD an opportunity to spend up to four months at the Institute in Halle (Saale), Germany, while completing their dissertations. The fellowships are offered by the Law Anthropology Department of the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology and are designed specifically for advanced doctoral researchers who are close to completing their manuscripts and whose research is directly relevant to the Department’s academic programme. For the 2027 cycle, fellows may choose between two possible residency periods: Spring 2027: March 1 to June 30, 2027 Fall 2027: September 1 to December 31, 2027 The fellowship may be awarded for a maximum of four months . Successful candidates will receive a monthly living stipend from the Institute. According to the announcement, the stipend is not taxable and is free of social security obligations . The exact stipend amount is not specified in the information provided. While applicants from relevant disciplinary backgrounds may be considered, the call explicitly states that priority will be given to candidates pursuing PhDs in anthropology . The application deadline is September 15, 2026 . About the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology The Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology , located in Halle (Saale), Germany, is an internationally recognized research institution specializing in social anthropology. Research at the Institute is broadly concerned with the comparative analysis of social change . Across its different programmes and projects, researchers investigate changing social relations, institutions, legal systems, political arrangements, cultural practices and economic structures. The Institute’s research contributes to anthropological theory while frequently engaging with questions that have significant practical, political and policy relevance. Its institutional setting provides doctoral and postdoctoral researchers with access to: An international scholarly community Research seminars Academic discussions Specialized expertise Institutional resources Interdisciplinary exchange Research networks For doctoral candidates finishing their dissertations, a short period of concentrated residence at the Institute can provide valuable time, intellectual engagement and access to a highly specialized research environment. About the Law Anthropology Department The fellowships are offered specifically by the Law Anthropology Department of the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology. The Department operates as an interdisciplinary space connecting: Social anthropology Legal anthropology Law Socio-legal studies Related interdisciplinary fields Its research is particularly concerned with the interactions among legal systems, communities, institutions and societies. The Department seeks to create a setting in which anthropologists and legal scholars can engage with one another and undertake research with both scholarly and policy relevance. Law, Society and Increasing Legal Pluralism One major intellectual concern of the Department is the increasing intensity of encounters between: Different legal systems National legal frameworks Communities Institutions Social groups Forms of normative ordering Contemporary societies are frequently characterized by overlapping legal systems and normative frameworks. These interactions can become especially visible in areas involving: Migration Religious law Family law International law Customary law Minority rights Citizenship Human rights Transnational communities Legal pluralism The Department is interested in research that helps explain these complex interactions empirically and theoretically. Empirically Grounded and Ethnographic Research The call emphasizes a growing demand for empirically grounded knowledge , particularly ethnographic research, about contemporary legal and social processes. Anthropological research can make important contributions because it examines not only what laws formally say, but how legal rules, institutions and normative expectations are actually experienced, interpreted and negotiated in everyday life. The Department is therefore particularly interested in research capable of connecting empirical findings with broader questions of: Law Policy Governance Rights Social transformation Institutional decision-making Translating Empirical Knowledge into Normative Thinking A central concern of the Law Anthropology Department is the challenge of translating empirically grounded research into forms of knowledge that can contribute to normative thinking and decision-making . The Department recognizes that anthropological findings and legal reasoning operate through different intellectual traditions. Nevertheless, there is growing demand for scholars who can help connect detailed empirical understanding with discussions occurring within: Policymaking Law Courts Governance institutions Civil society International organizations Public debate The Department therefore prioritizes research addressing this demand for translation, particularly within an increasingly plural European context. Applicants should carefully consider how their dissertation relates to this broader research agenda before applying. What Are the Dissertation Writing-up Fellowships? The fellowships are designed for doctoral researchers who have already completed most of their PhD research and are now working toward the finalization of the dissertation manuscript . They are not intended primarily to support: Beginning-stage doctoral students Major new fieldwork Initial research design Extensive new data collection Instead, the fellowship provides advanced doctoral candidates with a temporary academic base where they can focus on writing and completing their dissertations. The call specifically states that candidates should be in the final stage of their doctoral programme . Fellowship Duration Each fellowship may last for: Up to four months Applicants can choose between two fellowship periods. Spring Fellowship Period March 1 to June 30, 2027 This option may be particularly suitable for candidates expecting to complete their dissertations during the first half of 2027. Fall Fellowship Period September 1 to December 31, 2027 This provides a second opportunity for researchers whose dissertation schedules align better with the latter part of the year. The maximum duration remains four months. Financial Support Successful candidates will receive a: Monthly living stipend The Institute states that the stipend is: Not taxable Free of social security obligations The specific monthly amount is not stated in the information provided . Applicants should therefore avoid assuming a particular stipend value unless the Institute provides one directly through the application system or subsequent correspondence. What Fellows Are Expected to Do Although the principal purpose of the fellowship is dissertation completion, fellows are expected to engage actively with the Department during their residency. The fellowship is therefore not simply a private writing grant. Selected doctoral researchers should be prepared to: Work intensively on completing their dissertation Participate in Law Anthropology Department activities Contribute a working paper Present their doctoral research Engage with the Department’s scholarly community Participation in Department Activities Fellows are expected to take part in activities organized by the Law Anthropology Department during their fellowship period. These may provide opportunities to interact with: Senior researchers Visiting scholars Postdoctoral researchers Doctoral researchers Anthropologists Legal scholars Participation can help fellows receive intellectual feedback and situate their own research within broader interdisciplinary conversations. Working Paper Requirement Successful fellows are expected to submit: A working paper addressing the topic of their research This requirement demonstrates that the fellowship involves active academic contribution in addition to dissertation writing. Applicants should therefore be prepared to develop part of their dissertation research into a form suitable for circulation as a departmental working paper. Research Presentation Each fellow will also present their doctoral research as part of the Department’s: Seminar series This offers an opportunity to: Present findings Receive feedback Discuss methodology Refine arguments Engage with scholars from different disciplinary traditions Strengthen the final dissertation manuscript Applicants should therefore be comfortable discussing their research in an interdisciplinary academic setting. Relationship With the Home University One particularly important requirement concerns coordination between the Max Planck Institute and the candidate’s existing doctoral institution. Before the fellowship begins, a clear understanding must be reached between the Director of the Law Anthropology Department and the candidate’s principal doctoral supervisor . The purpose is to determine: How the candidate can make the fullest possible use of the writing period How the home university and Max Planck Institute can cooperate How the fellowship can contribute effectively to dissertation completion How the arrangement can benefit both institutions and the candidate This is important because the fellowship does not replace the candidate’s existing doctoral supervision. The researcher remains embedded in their home doctoral programme while spending a temporary period at the Max Planck Institute. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is intended for advanced doctoral candidates . Applicants should normally: Be enrolled in a doctoral programme Be in the final stage of the PhD Be sufficiently advanced to complete or substantially finalize the manuscript during the fellowship Have a dissertation topic immediately relevant to the Law Anthropology Department’s research programme Be able to spend up to four months at the Institute in Halle (Saale) Be willing to participate in departmental activities Be prepared to submit a working paper Be able to present their doctoral research during the Department seminar series Priority for Anthropology PhD Candidates For the 2027 call, the Department explicitly states that: Priority will be given to applicants working toward PhDs in anthropology. This does not necessarily mean that every applicant must be formally enrolled in an anthropology department. However, candidates whose projects are strongly grounded in anthropology, social anthropology or legal anthropology are likely to have the closest alignment with the call. Applicants from adjacent fields should make the anthropological or interdisciplinary relevance of their work especially clear. Research Fit Is Essential The candidate’s dissertation topic must be of immediate relevance to the Department’s research programme . This is a central requirement. Applicants should therefore avoid treating the fellowship as a general dissertation-writing opportunity available for any PhD topic. Before applying, candidates should review the research agenda of the Max Planck Institute and, in particular, the activities and publications associated with the Law Anthropology Department. A competitive applicant should be able to explain: How their dissertation connects to law and anthropology Why their research would benefit from the Department’s expertise What they could contribute to Department discussions Why a residency at the Institute is intellectually appropriate Examples of Potentially Relevant Research Themes The call itself does not provide an exhaustive list of acceptable dissertation topics. However, research fitting the Law Anthropology agenda may potentially engage with themes such as: Legal pluralism Anthropology of law Migration and law Human rights Religious law Customary law Minority rights Legal institutions Citizenship Governance Transnational legal processes Dispute resolution Social change and legal systems Empirical approaches to law Law and community Normative orders Legal translation European legal pluralism Applicants should not assume that every topic in this list is automatically eligible. The central requirement remains direct relevance to the Department’s current research programme. Application Materials Applicants must prepare several documents. 1. Cover Letter A cover letter is required. A strong cover letter should explain: Current doctoral status Dissertation topic Progress toward completion Why the Max Planck Institute is an appropriate environment How the research fits the Law Anthropology Department Which fellowship period is preferred What the applicant hopes to achieve during the residency The letter should make clear that the candidate is sufficiently advanced to benefit from a writing-up fellowship rather than still being in an exploratory research stage. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit an academic CV. The CV should clearly present: Education Doctoral programme Research experience Publications Conference presentations Teaching where relevant Research projects Grants and awards Relevant methodological skills Candidates should make their anthropological and law-related experience easy to identify. 3. Dissertation Writing Sample Applicants must submit: A chapter of the PhD dissertation This document gives reviewers direct evidence of: Academic writing ability Research quality Theoretical sophistication Methodological competence Dissertation progress Applicants should choose a chapter that best represents the quality and relevance of their doctoral research. 4. One-to-Two-Page Dissertation Summary Candidates must submit a: 1–2 page summary of the PhD work This summary should provide reviewers with a concise overview of the dissertation. It should ideally explain: Central research question Research context Theoretical framework Methodology Main argument Findings or emerging findings Contribution to the field Relevance to the Department Because reviewers will use this summary to understand the entire project quickly, clarity is especially important. 5. University Degrees and Transcripts Applicants must provide photocopies of: University degree certificates Academic transcripts These documents allow the selection committee to verify academic qualifications and background. 6. Supervisor Recommendation Letter A recommendation letter from the candidate’s: Principal doctoral supervisor is mandatory. The supervisor must specifically confirm that the applicant is: Advanced enough to finalize the doctoral manuscript within the period financed by the Law Anthropology Department. This is an important requirement because it directly verifies that the applicant has reached the appropriate dissertation stage. How the Recommendation Must Be Submitted The supervisor recommendation should be sent directly to the Department , rather than simply uploaded by the applicant. The specified email address is: marencakova@eth.mpg.de Candidates should contact their supervisors well before the application deadline so the recommendation can be prepared and submitted on time. Application Checklist Before submitting an application, candidates should make sure they have prepared: Cover letter Curriculum vitae Dissertation chapter as writing sample One-to-two-page dissertation summary Copies of university degrees Academic transcripts Supervisor recommendation letter sent directly to the Department Applicants should also ensure that their proposed research clearly fits the Law Anthropology Department’s research agenda. How to Apply Application materials must be submitted electronically through the Max Planck Institute’s official vacancy and recruitment system. Applicants can access vacancies through the Institute’s Career section or use the recruitment platform indicated in the call. More information: https://lnkd.in/dim6R52d Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology: http://www.eth.mpg.de Candidates should use the official online application system rather than sending the complete application directly by email unless specifically instructed otherwise. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline is: September 15, 2026 Applicants should ensure that both their own application materials and the supervisor recommendation are arranged well ahead of this date. Fellowship Timeline The two possible fellowship periods are: Spring 2027 March 1–June 30, 2027 Fall 2027 September 1–December 31, 2027 Each award can last for a maximum of four months. Contact for Application Questions Questions concerning the application process can be directed to: Carolin Klevenow Human Resources Management Email: klevenow@eth.mpg.de Applicants with administrative questions should use this contact rather than relying on unofficial information. Gender Equality and Diversity The Max Planck Society states that it strives to ensure: Gender equality Diversity Applicants from eligible backgrounds are therefore encouraged to consider the fellowship where their academic profile and dissertation topic match the programme. The supplied call does not state any gender-specific application restriction. Why This Fellowship Can Be Valuable Completing a dissertation can be one of the most demanding phases of doctoral study. By the final stage, researchers may already have: Completed fieldwork Gathered data Conducted archival research Finished major analysis Drafted several chapters Yet transforming these components into a coherent final manuscript requires sustained concentration. A dedicated writing fellowship can provide: Protected writing time Distance from routine obligations Access to scholarly resources New intellectual feedback Engagement with specialists Structured deadlines The Max Planck fellowship is especially valuable because it combines concentrated dissertation writing with integration into an internationally recognized research environment. Benefits of Spending the Fellowship at the Max Planck Institute Successful fellows will have the opportunity to use Institute resources while finalizing their dissertations. The intellectual environment may help candidates: Strengthen theoretical arguments Refine chapters Receive interdisciplinary feedback Develop future publications Build international scholarly connections Prepare for postdoctoral or academic careers The requirement to present research and prepare a working paper can also help fellows transform dissertation material into future scholarly outputs. Preparing a Competitive Application 1. Demonstrate That You Are Truly at the Writing-Up Stage This is perhaps the most important consideration. The fellowship is not aimed at students who still need extensive data collection or major fieldwork. Applicants should clearly show: What chapters are already drafted What research has been completed What remains to be written Why four months is sufficient to make substantial progress toward completion The supervisor recommendation must confirm this readiness. 2. Make Your Research Fit Explicit Do not assume that reviewers will identify your connection to the Department automatically. Clearly explain how your dissertation relates to: Law Anthropology Legal systems Social change Legal pluralism Translation between empirical and normative knowledge where applicable. 3. Explain Why Max Planck Is Necessary A strong application should communicate why spending four months in Halle would materially improve the dissertation. Possible reasons might include: Relevant faculty expertise Departmental research themes Interdisciplinary exchange Research resources Seminar participation Use reasons specific to your own project. 4. Select Your Writing Sample Carefully The dissertation chapter should showcase your strongest research and writing. Ideally, it should also demonstrate a close relationship with the Law Anthropology Department’s intellectual agenda. 5. title: Tulane University Postdoctoral Fellow 2027: 18-Month Position in Communication, Digital Media and the Future of Work
summary: Tulane University is inviting applications for an 18-month Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence , beginning on January 5, 2027 , in New Orleans, Louisiana. Hosted by the Department of Communication at Tulane University , the position is designed for early-career researchers whose scholarship examines the changing relationships between technology, society, politics, culture, digital media, influence, and the future of work . The selected Postdoctoral Fellow will become an inaugural affiliate of a developing interdisciplinary initiative focused on the future of work . Through both research and teaching, the Fellow will help contribute to the intellectual foundations of what Tulane describes as a prospective new interdisciplinary center. The role combines an active independent research agenda with undergraduate teaching, faculty mentorship, participation in departmental intellectual life, and access to Tulane University’s institutional and library resources. The appointment is full-time for 18 months and carries a 2-2 teaching load , meaning that the Fellow will teach two courses per semester. Tulane emphasizes that the position also includes protected research time so that the successful candidate can continue developing publications and a broader scholarly profile. Salary will be commensurate with experience , and the position includes a full benefits package. There is no fixed final application deadline stated in the vacancy. However, review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026 and continue until the position is filled . Candidates are therefore strongly encouraged to submit their materials before the first review date. About the Tulane University Postdoctoral Fellow Position The Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence is being recruited by Tulane University’s Department of Communication in anticipation of a broader interdisciplinary initiative examining the future of work . Rather than focusing on one narrow definition of work, the position welcomes researchers studying how contemporary changes in digital technologies, platforms, information systems, media, politics, and culture are transforming the way work is organized, experienced, governed, represented, and monetized. The successful Fellow will contribute through two complementary areas: Independent academic research Undergraduate teaching The Fellow will also participate in the intellectual development of the emerging future-of-work initiative. This makes the opportunity especially relevant to scholars interested in combining a traditional academic postdoctoral appointment with participation in a new institutional research agenda. Position at a Glance Institution: Tulane University Department: Communication Position: Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence Location: New Orleans, Louisiana, United States Employment: Full-time Appointment duration: 18 months Start date: January 5, 2027 Teaching load: Two courses per semester Research time: Protected research time included Salary: Commensurate with experience Benefits: Full benefits package Application review begins: October 15, 2026 Closing: Applications continue to be reviewed until the position is filled Contact: Dr. Vicki Mayer, vmayer@tulane.edu Research Focus: Technology, Society and the Future of Work Tulane is particularly interested in researchers whose work can advance critical debates concerning the ways the future of work intersects with technology, society, politics and culture . The call deliberately leaves room for a wide variety of substantive topics and methodological traditions. Potential research areas specifically identified by the Department include: Digital employment Work platforms Emerging and new technologies Big data applications Influence campaigns Advertising Political economy of attention Social media Digital policy Changing information environments Technology and labor Digital communication The list is illustrative rather than narrowly prescriptive. Applicants whose research connects meaningfully with the broader themes of digital communication, influence, emerging technologies and the future of work may therefore have a strong fit even if their exact project does not use one of these specific labels. Digital Employment and Work Platforms One potential research direction concerns the expansion of digitally mediated employment. Digital technologies increasingly organize how people: Find work Complete work Are managed Are evaluated Communicate professionally Develop careers Build professional identities Researchers examining digital labor or work platforms could therefore find this position particularly relevant. Potential topics could include platform economies, algorithmic management, remote work, digital labor, creator economies, online freelancing, gig work or changing relationships between workers and technological infrastructures. Tulane does not require applicants to work on any one of these topics, but digital employment is specifically included among the areas of interest. Emerging and New Technologies The future-of-work initiative also welcomes scholarship examining new and emerging technologies. This could potentially include research on technological developments affecting: Communication Employment Management Media production Information circulation Organizational culture Political communication Advertising Public discourse Because the position is situated in Communication, applicants should be able to demonstrate how their work contributes to questions relevant to media, communication, influence, technology or related social processes. Big Data Applications Big data is another research area highlighted by the Department. Researchers may investigate how large-scale data systems are reshaping communication, organizations, platforms, labor practices, surveillance, targeting or decision-making. Potential questions could involve: Data-driven management Algorithmic systems Digital surveillance Data analytics Targeted advertising Platform governance Data and workplace power Again, these are potential directions rather than formal requirements. Influence Campaigns and Advertising The position places particular emphasis on influence . Researchers working on advertising, persuasion, political communication, digital influence, information campaigns or platform-based communication may therefore be particularly well aligned. Influence can operate across multiple areas, including: Political campaigns Commercial advertising Social-media promotion Digital persuasion Branding Influencer cultures Public communication Organizational communication The successful Fellow may investigate these topics through critical, qualitative, quantitative, computational, historical or mixed-method approaches. Political Economy of Attention Tulane also identifies the political economy of attention as a relevant research area. The contemporary digital environment increasingly treats attention as an economic and political resource. Researchers may examine how platforms, advertisers, media institutions, creators, employers and other actors compete for and monetize attention. This could raise questions about: Platform capitalism Advertising systems Algorithmic visibility Monetization Digital labor Audience measurement Media industries Economic power Candidates whose scholarship examines media and communication through political-economic perspectives could therefore be strong potential applicants. Social Media Research Social media represents another major research area. Potential applicants may investigate how social platforms shape: Work Professional identity Politics Influence Advertising Labor Public culture Information Social relationships Research could potentially focus on major platforms, emerging media ecosystems or broader social and institutional consequences of platformization. Digital Policy Tulane also welcomes scholars working on digital policy . Relevant questions could include: Platform regulation Data governance Digital rights Online advertising regulation Technology policy Labor regulation Artificial intelligence governance Information policy Platform accountability This area could be particularly relevant to applicants interested in bridging academic research with policy debates. All Methodological Approaches Are Welcome One of the notable features of the vacancy is that Tulane explicitly welcomes: All methodological approaches The Department therefore does not require applicants to use one particular form of research. Potential approaches may include: Qualitative research Quantitative research Mixed methods Computational methods Ethnography Interviews Archival research Historical analysis Textual analysis Discourse analysis Policy analysis Digital methods Critical theory Applicants should select methods appropriate to their own scholarly questions. This methodological openness creates space for candidates from a wide range of intellectual traditions within Communication and adjacent disciplines. Research Expectations The successful Fellow is expected to maintain an active research agenda throughout the 18-month appointment . Tulane will provide several forms of institutional support. These include: Faculty mentorship Workshop participation opportunities Institutional resources Library resources Departmental colloquia Working groups The Fellow will be encouraged to use the appointment to advance their research and publication profile. Publication Expectations The position specifically encourages Fellows to submit scholarly work for publication. This could include developing: Journal articles Book chapters Manuscripts Conference papers Collaborative research The vacancy does not specify a mandatory publication quota. Instead, the emphasis is on maintaining active scholarly productivity appropriate to an early-career academic. Protected Research Time Despite the teaching responsibilities, Tulane emphasizes that the Fellow will have protected research time . This is significant because the appointment is intended to support both teaching development and scholarly advancement. Applicants should therefore consider how they would use the 18-month period to move their research agenda forward. A strong application may benefit from explaining: Current research projects Planned publications Future research questions How Tulane’s environment would support the work How the proposed scholarship relates to the future-of-work initiative Teaching Responsibilities The Fellow will teach: Two courses per semester This represents a 2-2 teaching load . The teaching responsibilities are divided conceptually into two areas. Course 1: Fellow’s Research or Methodological Expertise One course will reflect the Fellow’s own: Research specialization Methodological expertise This provides the successful applicant with an opportunity to design or teach material closely connected to their scholarship. Depending on the Fellow’s background, this course could potentially focus on areas such as digital labor, social media, political communication, advertising, platforms, digital research methods, media industries or other relevant subjects. Course 2: Contemporary Digital Communication and Influence The second course will address topics connected with contemporary changes in communication and information. Potential areas identified in the job description include: Digital communication Media influence Advertising Information Persuasion Changing communication landscapes The Department describes these as topics important to students’ knowledge and skills as they prepare for future careers. This means the successful candidate should be able to connect academic research with practical and contemporary questions facing students entering media, communication, policy, technology or related professions. Ability to Teach Undergraduates Effective undergraduate teaching is an explicit qualification. Applicants should therefore demonstrate evidence of teaching ability where possible. This could include: Courses previously taught Teaching assistantships Guest lectures Course design Teaching evaluations Pedagogical training Mentoring students Applicants without extensive independent teaching experience should still clearly articulate their capacity and readiness to teach at the undergraduate level. PhD Requirement Applicants must hold a: PhD in Communication or a closely related discipline The doctorate must be conferred by January 5, 2027 , the start date of the appointment. This means candidates who are currently completing their doctorate may apply as long as all requirements will be completed and the degree formally conferred by the appointment date. Candidates whose PhD will not be completed by January 5, 2027 would not satisfy the published requirement. What Counts as a Closely Related Discipline? The vacancy does not provide an exhaustive list of acceptable related fields. Potentially relevant disciplines could include areas intersecting closely with Communication, digital media, technology, media studies, political communication or related social-science and humanities research. However, applicants from outside Communication should ensure that their research demonstrates a clear intellectual fit with: Digital communication Media Influence Advertising Future of work Technology and society Candidates uncertain about disciplinary fit can direct questions to Dr. Vicki Mayer. Required Research Specialization Applicants must demonstrate research specialization in: Digital communication Influence Advertising or a closely related area. This requirement reinforces the importance of showing a coherent intellectual connection between the applicant’s previous research and the position. A candidate who works broadly on technology or society should explain clearly how their project contributes to the Department’s communication-centered agenda. Scholarly Productivity The successful candidate should demonstrate: Evidence of scholarly productivity commensurate with career stage This wording recognizes that postdoctoral applicants may have different publication records depending on when they completed or are completing their PhDs. Relevant evidence could include: Peer-reviewed articles Book chapters Manuscripts under review Conference presentations Published research Significant working papers Other scholarly outputs Candidates should organize their CV so that reviewers can easily identify their strongest research achievements. Preferred Qualification: Interdisciplinary Engagement Tulane is particularly interested in someone willing to contribute to campus-wide discussions concerning the development of the new interdisciplinary center. This suggests that the successful Fellow should be comfortable collaborating beyond the Communication Department. The future of work is inherently interdisciplinary and can involve scholarship from areas such as: Communication Sociology Political science Economics Business Technology studies Media studies Cultural studies Labor studies Public policy Applicants who can communicate across disciplinary boundaries may therefore be particularly competitive. Community-Engaged Research Experience with community-engaged research is considered a plus. Community-engaged scholarship may involve conducting research collaboratively with communities, organizations or practitioners rather than treating them only as research subjects. This type of experience could be particularly relevant in New Orleans, where questions concerning work, technology, culture, media, inequality and urban life may intersect in complex ways. However, community-engaged research is preferred rather than required. Policy-Relevant Research Experience producing policy-relevant research is also considered advantageous. Researchers whose scholarship contributes to conversations around digital governance, platform regulation, information policy, advertising, labor or technology policy may therefore have an additional point of alignment. This may be particularly relevant for scholars who want their work to engage audiences beyond academia. Compensation and Benefits The salary is described as: Commensurate with experience No specific salary range is provided in the supplied vacancy. Location The position is based at: Tulane University in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States This is not described as a remote position. Applicants should therefore expect to relocate to or work in New Orleans for the appointment unless Tulane provides a different arrangement during the hiring process. Application Materials Candidates must submit several materials through the official application system. 1. Cover Letter Applicants should provide a cover letter describing: Research agenda Fit with the position The cover letter is likely to be one of the most important opportunities to explain the connection between the applicant’s existing work and Tulane’s emerging future-of-work initiative. title: Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator 2026: WFP Climate Innovation Opportunity for Scalable Solutions in Latin America and the Caribbean
summary: The Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator (AFCIA) 2026 , implemented by the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) Innovation Accelerator in partnership with the Adaptation Fund , is inviting organizations with innovative climate adaptation solutions to apply for support to strengthen resilience, improve food security and help vulnerable communities respond to climate change. The opportunity is particularly focused on Latin America and the Caribbean , with this edition seeking solutions that can be implemented in or have strong potential for implementation in the Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Peru . Applications are open to established organizations developing solutions that address pressing climate adaptation challenges, including climate-smart agriculture, early warning systems, climate information, disaster risk management, water management, climate-risk financing and post-harvest losses. Application deadline: 6 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC. What Is the Main Goal of the Programme? The AFCIA programme aims to support innovations that can contribute to a more resilient and sustainable future for communities facing climate-related challenges. The programme seeks to: Strengthen climate adaptation and resilience. Improve food security. Support vulnerable and climate-affected communities. Promote gender equity and inclusion. Create inclusive economic opportunities. Engage young people in climate adaptation. Encourage collaboration between innovators and humanitarian organizations. Expand knowledge and learning around climate adaptation. Support solutions with potential for large-scale implementation. Promote sustainable and locally relevant approaches to climate resilience. Rather than focusing only on ideas at an early conceptual stage, the programme is seeking innovations that have already progressed beyond the idea or early pre-seed phase and have a credible pathway toward implementation and scale. What Types of Innovations Is WFP Looking For? The programme is open to both low-tech and high-tech solutions . This means applicants do not necessarily need to have developed sophisticated or highly technical technologies. What matters is whether the innovation provides a meaningful, scalable and sustainable response to a clearly identified climate adaptation challenge. Potential solutions may involve: Digital technologies Climate information systems Agricultural technologies Early-warning systems Financing mechanisms Water-management approaches Climate-smart agriculture Disaster-risk management Food-system innovations Market intelligence Communication technologies Community-based approaches Humanitarian innovations Environmental solutions Business-model innovations The most important consideration is whether the proposed solution addresses a relevant climate adaptation problem and has credible potential for impact and scale. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is designed for established legal entities , rather than individual applicants. Eligible organizations may include: For-profit companies Non-profit organizations Social businesses NGOs International NGOs Other established legal entities An organization must also have a presence in at least one of the three countries of implementation: Dominican Republic, El Salvador or Peru . This presence could include: A country office A permanent operational presence A subsidiary Long-term operations An established partnership in the country Organizations from outside the three countries may therefore be relevant if they have an appropriate and established presence or partnership structure in one of the target countries. Key Eligibility Requirements Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before applying. The innovation must: 1. Be submitted by an established legal entity The applicant must be an established organization such as a company, NGO, social business or other legally recognized entity. 2. Have a presence in a target country The organization should have an established presence in: Dominican Republic El Salvador Peru 3. Address a relevant climate adaptation challenge The innovation must respond to at least one of the priority areas identified for the country where it will be implemented. 4. Be beyond the idea stage The innovation must be at least at the seed stage . Solutions that are still only ideas, research concepts or at the early pre-seed stage are not eligible. 5. Have potential for scale Applicants should demonstrate a clear pathway for expanding their solution beyond a small pilot. 6. Have adequate resources The organization must have sufficient resources and capabilities to implement the proposed activities during the nine-month Sprint programme using the available funding. 7. Demonstrate willingness to collaborate Applicants are expected to have strong intentions to: Collaborate with relevant humanitarian stakeholders Develop relationships with WFP country offices Engage with local innovation ecosystems Work with relevant partners How Will Innovations Be Evaluated? Eligible applications will be assessed against several important criteria. 1. Level of Innovation The proposed solution should demonstrate genuine innovation and respond effectively to climate adaptation challenges within the identified thematic areas. WFP will consider how novel and innovative the solution is and whether it offers a meaningful improvement over existing approaches. 2. Relevance to the Local Context The solution must be relevant to at least one of the target countries and its identified climate adaptation priorities. Applicants should demonstrate: A clear understanding of the problem The relevance of the solution The needs of intended users How the innovation fits the local ecosystem The practical value of the solution 3. Financial Sustainability and Scalability A strong application should demonstrate that the innovation can become financially sustainable. Applicants should be able to explain: How the solution generates or can generate sustainable revenue How it can continue beyond programme support What its business model looks like How the solution can grow What resources will be required for expansion Scalability is an important part of the opportunity because the programme is looking for innovations capable of generating meaningful impact beyond a limited pilot. 4. Team Expertise and Capabilities The strength of the team will also be considered. Applicants should demonstrate: Relevant technical expertise Entrepreneurial capabilities Commitment Motivation Ability to implement the proposed solution Technical coherence Appropriate leadership Diverse and inclusive team composition A strong solution must be supported by a team capable of turning the proposed innovation into measurable results. 5. Climate Adaptation The innovation should make a meaningful contribution to climate adaptation. This could involve: Increasing resilience to climate impacts Improving resource efficiency Promoting sustainable practices Helping communities prepare for climate-related shocks Supporting adaptive decision-making Reducing vulnerability to climate risks 6. Level of Impact Applicants should provide evidence of the solution s actual or potential impact. WFP will consider whether the innovation can produce: Tangible results Sustainable improvements Long-term benefits Meaningful climate adaptation outcomes Improvements that can extend beyond the grant or programme period Historical evidence of impact can strengthen an application, particularly where the innovation has already been tested. 7. Environmental and Social Sustainability Solutions must align with the environmental and social principles of the Adaptation Fund . Applicants should therefore consider the broader environmental and social implications of their proposed innovation. 8. Gender and Inclusion Gender equality and inclusion are important components of the programme. Applicants should demonstrate how their solution: Addresses diverse user needs Promotes inclusive participation Supports inclusive decision-making Uses disaggregated data where appropriate Incorporates feedback from different user groups Considers the needs of populations that may be disproportionately affected by climate change Application Process Interested organizations should first carefully review the official call for applications and eligibility requirements. The application process involves completing the online application form and providing information about the organization, the innovation, the problem being addressed, the target market or users, the solution s impact and its potential for scale. The three countries specifically identified are: Dominican Republic El Salvador Peru What is the deadline? The stated deadline is 6 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC . Selected applicants will be invited to the innovation bootcamp, after which teams have an opportunity to apply for the Sprint programme and associated funding. When will successful applications be announced? The programme information indicates that approximately 10–12 successful applications are expected to be selected in November 2026 . When is the bootcamp? The innovation bootcamp is scheduled for January 2027 . Are both technology and non-technology solutions eligible? Read the Official AFCIA 2026 Call for Applications After confirming eligibility, applicants can complete the official online application form: Apply to the AFCIA 2026 Programme Applicants should submit their application before 6 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC . APPLY HERE Conclusion The Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator 2026 represents an important opportunity for established organizations developing practical climate adaptation solutions with potential to improve resilience, food security and livelihoods. The current call focuses on the Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Peru , with priority areas ranging from climate-smart agriculture and disaster risk management to early-warning systems, climate information, water management, climate-risk financing and post-harvest loss reduction. title: Climate Caucus Programs & Policy Senior Manager 2026: Fully Remote Climate Policy Role Paying $75,000–$80,000 Per Year
