summary: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 Are you passionate about Africa’s development, leadership, public policy, education, entrepreneurship, community development, or the long-term vision of The Africa We Want ? The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers an opportunity to take part in a structured seven-week online learning and volunteer experience designed to help participants understand how they can contribute to Africa’s transformation within their own spheres of influence. Hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and delivered through the wider Agenda 2063 learning ecosystem, the programme focuses on turning knowledge of Agenda 2063 into practical individual leadership and action. The online assignment is designed for people who want to explore their personal contribution to Africa’s development while supporting other participants during the seven-week traineeship. It does not require applicants to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. Instead, it emphasizes curiosity, critical engagement, communication, willingness to learn, and the ability to help others connect ideas to their own real-world environments. Opportunity Overview Opportunity Title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 Host Entity: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Assignment Country: Ethiopia Modality: Online Duration: 7 weeks Time Commitment: 11–15 hours per week Task Type: Development of plans Relevant Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals Expected Start Date: The listing does not provide a valid start date Number of Assignments: 0 as indicated in the provided listing Language: English, fluent level desirable Deadline: No application deadline is specified in the provided opportunity details What Is Agenda 2063? Agenda 2063 is Africa’s long-term development framework and vision for building “The Africa We Want.” It provides a continental framework for transforming Africa economically, socially and politically while promoting inclusive development, sustainable growth, integration and stronger partnerships. However, understanding Agenda 2063 as a policy or development framework is only one part of the challenge. Its implementation also depends on the actions of individuals and institutions operating in different environments. This is the central idea behind Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces . The programme recognizes that important decisions are made every day in many different environments, including: Governments and public institutions Businesses and private-sector organizations Universities and research institutions Schools and educational organizations Communities and civil society Development organizations Families Professional networks Entrepreneurship and innovation spaces Youth organizations Other environments where people make decisions and create value These environments are described as “Power Spaces.” The programme encourages participants to identify the Power Spaces available to them and consider how they can deliberately use those spaces to contribute to Africa’s long-term transformation. What Is Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3? Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is a seven-week online traineeship and volunteer learning experience designed to move participants beyond simply knowing about Agenda 2063. The programme seeks to help participants answer an important question: How can I personally contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the spaces in which I have influence? Rather than treating leadership as something limited to senior government officials, executives or institutional leaders, the programme takes a broader approach. It recognizes that individuals can create value and influence outcomes from wherever they operate. A student can influence a university or student organization. An entrepreneur can influence a business ecosystem. A teacher can influence learners and communities. A researcher can influence policy and knowledge. A community leader can influence local development. A communications professional can influence public awareness and engagement. The programme therefore focuses on developing individual agency and helping participants recognize themselves as potential contributors to Agenda 2063. Main Objective of the Programme The central objective is to help participants progress from understanding Agenda 2063 to recognizing themselves as agents capable of contributing to its implementation . The seven-week journey provides a structured framework through which participants examine: The value they currently create. The future they want to help create. The changes required to move from the present toward that future. The leadership values required to make meaningful decisions. The routines needed to turn intentions into action. The future they want to experience as a result of their efforts. The lessons they gain and the changes they need to make going forward. This makes the programme particularly relevant to people interested in leadership, development practice, public policy, entrepreneurship, education, community development and African transformation. The Seven Leadership Tools Participants Will Develop One of the most important features of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is its seven-tool leadership architecture. Throughout the seven-week journey, participants progressively work with seven leadership tools. 1. Contribution Statement – What Value Do I Create? The first tool encourages participants to identify their personal contribution to Africa’s transformation. Participants examine their current Power Space and consider the value they create within it. This may involve asking questions such as: What am I currently contributing? Who benefits from my contribution? What capabilities do I possess? What problems am I helping to solve? Where do I have influence? How does my work or activity connect with Africa’s broader development needs? The Contribution Statement helps participants understand where they currently fit within the broader transformation agenda. 2. Moonshot – What Future Am I Committed to Creating? The second tool focuses on developing a sufficiently ambitious vision for the future. The concept of a “Moonshot” encourages participants to think beyond incremental improvements and identify a consequential future they are committed to helping create. Participants consider: What future do I want to see? What would meaningful transformation look like? What ambitious outcome would challenge current assumptions? What future is worth working toward despite present obstacles? The exercise is intended to help participants challenge the limitations imposed by present circumstances. 3. Delivery – What Must Change? Having identified a desired future, participants then examine what needs to change to move toward it. The Delivery tool focuses on the gap between the current situation and the desired outcome. Participants may consider: What is preventing progress? Which systems, behaviours or practices need to change? What obstacles must be addressed? Which changes are most critical? What actions can contribute to the desired transformation? This stage helps translate vision into a practical understanding of what needs to happen. 4. Leadership Values – Who Must I Be? The fourth tool focuses on the personal qualities and values required to pursue meaningful change. Participants reflect on the type of leader they need to become in order to make consequential decisions and remain committed to their goals. This can involve examining: Personal values Integrity Responsibility Courage Accountability Resilience Collaboration Commitment Respect for others Willingness to learn and adapt The emphasis is not simply on what participants want to achieve but also on who they need to be throughout the journey. 5. Leadership Routines – What Must I Repeatedly Do? A vision only becomes meaningful when it is translated into consistent action. The Leadership Routines tool helps participants identify repeated behaviours and practices that can gradually produce results. Participants consider: What actions must I perform consistently? Which habits will support my goals? What behaviours need to become routine? How can I turn intention into practice? What repeated actions can accumulate into meaningful results? This stage emphasizes the importance of sustained action rather than one-time motivation. 6. Letter from the Future – What Does Life Look Like Because I Succeeded? The sixth tool asks participants to imagine their desired future as though they have already achieved it. Through a Letter from the Future , participants explore what life looks like because their efforts succeeded. This exercise can help participants: Visualize the impact of their contribution. Understand the consequences of achieving their goals. Reconsider current choices. Identify actions that are consistent with their desired future. Strengthen their connection to their long-term objectives. The exercise links future aspirations with present-day decision-making. 7. Future Review – What Have I Learned and What Should I Now Revise? The final tool focuses on reflection, learning and continuous improvement. Participants are introduced to the practice of: Return → Review → Revise → Recommit This process encourages participants to revisit their leadership plans and assess whether their circumstances, experiences and capabilities have changed.
